members.ItemEquippable.GetClassAmmoInPackAbs(SNe: RVA 0x1324EF0, dumpLine 565109 — the rounds the item's own class pool still holds in the pack

toolAmmo.whyThisIsTheToolEnergy: the class pool is the pool the game spends for the item's own category: a tool draws its energy from it and a weapon its class reserve, and PlayerNativeSources.cs already reads it as `reserve` for v-p-ammo
toolAmmo.poolShape: Player.PlayerAmmoStorage holds one InventorySlotAmmo per pool (StandardAmmo/SpecialAmmo/ClassAmmo/ResourcePackAmmo/ConsumableAmmo, dumpLines 658010-658014); InventorySlotAmmo.BulletsInPack is the bullet count and AmmoInPack/CostOfBullet is how the game derives it

members.PlayerBackpack.PocketItemsGroups: List<List<PocketItem>> (+0x38), dumpLine 658210 — one inner list per item id, which is the stack the pickup and removal paths maintain
members.PlayerBackpack.ItemIDToPocketItemGroup: Dictionary<uint, List<PocketItem>> (+0x40), dumpLine 658211 — the same stacks keyed by item id
members.PlayerBackpack.CountPocketItem(uint item: RVA 0x175EDC0, dumpLine 658308 — one item's stack size, the read the inventory consume row already uses for its readback

consumables.whatTheRowAnswers: `count` is the number of items across the backpack's pocket stacks and `stacks` is how many stacks they are grouped into; both are read from PocketItemsGroups at the same moment as the two ammunition numbers, so the five ports describe one sample
consumables.perItemNarrowing: reading one named item's stack (`CountPocketItem(itemID)`) needs the item's own id, which a plan can only name through the `forge.resource.item` half no provider registers in this runtime; the row therefore promises the stacks the backpack really holds and does not declare a port nothing could fill. When that resource half lands, the same native member answers a per-item row with no new read

row.kindNote: ruling 102 converts every `forge.query.*` value row to `kind: state` with `execution: query` in the integration batch, together with the registration whitelist that currently refuses a `state` row at the query tier (RuntimeRegistry.WithModule registers an evaluator only for selector/condition/modifier, and RuntimePlan accepts the same three for a `query` node). This row declares the kind the framework accepts today, exactly like the seven player value rows beside it, and travels in that conversion
row.reads: one budgeted snapshot through the kernel's query session, then one native read by this provider's own half; both come from the life the snapshot just verified

refusals.no-wielded-gear: the player holds nothing, so there is no pool this row can name
refusals.equipment-unresolved: the held item exists but no registered package can name it as an entity
refusals.backpack-unavailable: the player's backpack could not be read
refusals.readback-exception: a pool read threw, or answered outside its own bounds (negative rounds, a cap of zero, more rounds than the cap)
